- Model consistently underestimates prices after initial spikes or strong sentiment shifts (e.g., sentiment > 0.00 in recent days).
- Forecasts tend to be too flat or linear, failing to capture sharp upward momentum in early periods (e.g., 2022-11-23 to 2022-12-01).
- Overshoots occur after spikes, especially when sentiment is low or neutral (e.g., 2022-12-02, 2022-12-05).
- Mean reversion is overestimated — model often predicts continued rise after peak, ignoring volatility decay.
- Forecasts lag behind true price movements by 1–2 days, especially when sentiment is positive or volatile.
- When sentiment is > 0.00 in recent history, model should adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect bullish momentum.
- After a sharp spike (e.g., > 5% from prior day), model should reduce slope or cap growth to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is 0.00 for 3+ consecutive days, model should not assume upward trend — consider downward bias or flat path.
- Forecasts should be adjusted downward if true outcome shows early correction or mean reversion within 3–5 days.
- Model overestimates long-term trend when sentiment is low — should cap growth to 1–2% per day unless sentiment > 0.20.
